articles.title: Dak Prescott honors late mother and brother through charity work as Faith Fight Finish Foundation raises $1.5 million
articles.summary: For Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, helping others is about more than giving money to charity.
articles.body: For Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, helping others is about more than giving money to charity. His work comes from two painful losses that changed his life. His mother, Peggy Prescott, died from colon cancer in 2013, and his older brother, Jace Prescott, died by suicide in 2020. Both losses became part of the reason he created the Faith Fight Finish Foundation, which supports cancer research, mental health awareness, suicide prevention and families going through difficult times. Over the years, Prescott has used his success in the NFL to raise money, support community programs and help people who are facing struggles similar to those his own family experienced.Why did Dak Prescott start the Faith Fight Finish Foundation?Prescott established the Faith Fight Finish Foundation to honour his mother, Peggy, whose words of encouragement helped shape his life. The name comes from the three words that became important to their family: faith, fight and finish.Peggy died from colon cancer in 2013, when Prescott was a student at Mississippi State University. Her experience with the disease showed him how difficult cancer treatment can be for patients and their families. The foundation later expanded its work to honour his brother Jace, whose death by suicide in 2020 pushed Prescott to speak more openly about mental health.The foundation focuses on four main areas: colon cancer research, mental health and suicide prevention, improving relationships between law enforcement and communities, and helping families facing serious hardships.Rather than limiting its work to awareness campaigns, the organisation also provides practical help. According to its official website, it supports families dealing with medical emergencies by helping cover expenses such as travel, housing, groceries and other basic living costs that insurance may not pay for. This can allow families to focus on treatment instead of worrying about every expense.How much money has Dak Prescott invested in charity?There is no complete, publicly confirmed figure showing how much of his personal wealth Prescott has invested in philanthropy over the years. However, several reported donations and fundraising efforts offer a clearer picture of the money connected to his charitable work.In 2019, his foundation funded the first Peggy Prescott Early Career Scientist Award in Colorectal Cancer Research with a $50,000 grant through Stand Up To Cancer. The award supported researcher Karin Pelka of the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, whose work focused on understanding how immune cells affect responses to cancer treatment.Prescott also pledged $1 million toward police training, education and advocacy following the killing of George Floyd in 2020. The foundation says this initiative aims to improve relationships between law enforcement officers and the communities they serve.During the COVID-19 pandemic, Faith Fight Finish reported providing nearly $65,000 in grants to organisations supporting people affected by the health crisis and first responders. The foundation also helped provide protective equipment and disinfecting supplies to fire departments in Louisiana.More recently, Prescott made two reported contributions of $125,000 each in 2024 and 2025 to support cancer-related causes in his home community, according to the LSU Health Shreveport Foundation’s June 2025 newsletter. One contribution supported colon cancer screenings through its Partners in Wellness vans, while the other went toward the McDade House campaign.These figures represent selected contributions and pledges, not a confirmed total of Prescott’s personal charitable spending. Some money comes through his foundation, fundraising events and partnerships, so it would be inaccurate to describe every amount as a direct personal donation.How is his foundation helping people with cancer and mental health problems?Cancer research remains one of the foundation’s central priorities because of Peggy’s experience. Through its partnership with Stand Up To Cancer, the organisation continues to support research into colorectal cancer. The goal is to help scientists improve understanding of the disease and develop better approaches to treatment.The foundation also works to make early detection more accessible. Prescott’s contributions to cancer screening programmes in Louisiana are one example of how his charitable work can help people access medical services, rather than focusing only on research funding.Mental health and suicide prevention are equally important to him. Following Jace’s death, Prescott became more vocal about the need to discuss emotional struggles and seek help. His foundation has partnered with The Defensive Line, the nonprofit co-founded by NFL player Solomon Thomas, to support workshops for middle and high school educators.These workshops help teachers recognise signs of emotional distress, understand suicide prevention and connect students with appropriate support. The foundation has also worked with the Kevin Love Fund on programmes that help young people understand their emotions and feel more comfortable discussing mental health.Its work with the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention has also helped raise awareness of crisis support resources, including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in the United States.Prescott’s approach is personal, but the aim is practical: help people recognise when someone is struggling and make it easier for them to find support before a crisis becomes worse.How much did his latest charity Gala Raise, and where does the money go?Prescott’s foundation also raises money through fundraising events that bring together supporters, business leaders and other public figures. At its fifth annual gala on July 17, 2026, Faith Fight Finish raised $1.5 million to support its work, according to People Newspapers.The event included a performance by country music star Kane Brown and highlighted the foundation’s four main areas of work. The money raised was intended to further its mission of supporting cancer research, mental health and suicide prevention, police-community relations, and families facing serious hardships.The foundation’s earlier work also shows how its support reaches beyond large fundraising events. It has helped families affected by medical emergencies, supported youth programmes and covered funeral expenses for a young football player who died while attending Prescott’s former high school.Prescott has also received recognition for his community work. He won the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award for the 2022 season. The award came with a $250,000 donation to his foundation, according to the Dallas Cowboys’ media guide.His charitable work does not erase the losses he has experienced, but it gives those experiences a purpose beyond his own family. articles.title: Travis Hunter becomes first player in 24 years to have an INT and receiving TD in the same game
articles.summary: Hunter had a 7-yard TD in the fourth quarter against the Texans, and then picked off C.J. Stroud on the next drive.
articles.body:
Travis Hunter finally delivered the dual-threat performance he insisted he could achieve in the NFL in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans .

Hunter left college determined to keep playing both sides of the ball. After his rookie season, head coach Liam Coen committed to having Hunter play mostly defense, with sporadic snaps on offense.

On Sunday against the Houston Texans, the dual-threat player etched his name into the history books with an interception and a receiving touchdown.

Hunter caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence early in the fourth quarter.

On the next drive, Hunter picked off Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud.

The Jaguars WR/CB combo became only the third player in Super Bowl history to do so. Before Hunter, the most recent was Brian Dawkins, also ironically against the Texans. The only other player in the Super Bowl era to have an interception and receiving touchdown in the same game was Roy Green in 1981 for the then-St. Louis Cardinals.

Unfortunately for Hunter, the Jaguars lost on a field goal as time expired. The dual-threat player finished with 59 yards and a touchdown on four receptions. He also had three tackles and an interception on defense.

Hunter played in seven games as a rookie. He finished with 298 yards and a touchdown on offense and 15 tackles on defense. Hunter played 67% of offensive snaps and 36% of defensive snaps.

This year, those snap counts have almost flipped. Through five games, heading into Sunday's game against Houston, Hunter had played 79% of defensive snaps and just 7% of offensive snaps.

As a wide receiver this year, he caught 2 passes for 17 yards on 21 offensive snaps. On defense, Hunter had his first career interception in Week 3 against the New England Patriots. He played 100% of defensive snaps in Weeks 4 and 5.

articles.title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Evaluated for Apparent Ankle Injury on Sideline vs. Bucs
articles.summary: It's not too often an NFL head coach spends time in the blue medical tent, but that's what happened for Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
It's not too often an NFL head coach spends time in the blue medical tent, but that's what happened for Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Christopher Carter of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported McCarthy spent halftime in the tent with what appeared to be a sprained ankle. He was seen limping and never went into the locker room to address his team.

ESPN's Brooke Pryor noted he was on the sideline with his playsheet in hand to start the second half, so he seemed to avoid a serious setback.

There wasn't much that went right for McCarthy and the Steelers in the first half, as Tampa Bay largely controlled play and took a 13-3 lead into the locker room.

Emeka Egbuka caught the only touchdown of the first half, and Pittsburgh was left in comeback mode even with Baker Mayfield sidelined for the Buccaneers.

The AFC North team entered play with a 3-2 record.

It is McCarthy's first season as the head coach of the Steelers after leading the Green Bay Packers for 13 seasons and the Dallas Cowboys for five. He coached Rodgers with the Packers and was reunited with the future Hall of Famer in Pittsburgh for the 2026 campaign.

Fortunately for the head coach and his team, he seemed to avoid any serious injuries and was back on the sidelines to start the second half.

articles.title: Alvin Kamara Joins Exclusive NFL Club with Rare Statistical Milestone in Saints vs. Giants
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints star running back Alvin Kamara joined elite company during Sunday's game against the New York Giants.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints star running back Alvin Kamara joined elite company during Sunday's game against the New York Giants.

After his 31-yard touchdown reception early in the third quarter, Kamara became the sixth player in NFL history to record 5,000 rushing and receiving yards in his career.

Kamara entered Sunday's game with 7,336 career rushing yards and 4,989 career receiving yards. His touchdown reception broke a 10-10 tie after the Saints stormed back from a 10-0 deficit.

Kamara has never recorded a 1,000-yard rushing or receiving season in his career, but his dual-threat ability allowed him to still become one of the best running backs of his generation. The 31-year-old has been selected to the Pro Bowl five times, and he's earned second-team All-Pro honors twice.

Kamara has been off to a slow start this season, entering Sunday's matchup with 86 rushing yards and 41 receiving yards. He's tied for the team lead with two rushing touchdowns, but it's clear that it's been an adjustment to share the backfield with Travis Etienne.

Despite opening the year with a 1-4 record, the Saints still have a chance to get back into the race for the NFC South. The Carolina Panthers currently lead the division with a 2-2 record, so there's still a path to bounce back if New Orleans can string together some wins.

Kamara and the Saints will try to finish off Sunday's comeback against the Giants after the star ball-carrier achieved history.

articles.title: Kendal Daniels Released from Hospital After Scary Injury, Latest Updates on Falcons LB
articles.summary: A scary scene unfolded in the third quarter of Sunday's game between the Atlanta Falcons and Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
A scary scene unfolded in the third quarter of Sunday's game between the Atlanta Falcons and Chicago Bears.

Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels suffered an injury on a tackle attempt and remained on the field until he was stabilized and loaded onto a cart on a gurney. Players from both teams surrounded him on the field as trainers were on the scene during the stoppage, which lasted for several minutes.

According to the Falcons , Daniels "is alert and has movement in all his extremities." He was transported to Memorial Hospital for further evaluation.

He was later able to return to the stadium while walking on his own power, according to multiple reporters:

The injury happened when Daniels' facemask collided with Colston Loveland's knee on a tackle attempt.

Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk noted medical personnel cut his jersey off during the process of immobilizing his neck.

Smith added that the linebacker "appeared to be conscious and moving a hand."

He was the second linebacker who was wearing the green dot helmet and calling the defensive plays to leave the game for the Falcons. Divine Deablo initially left the contest with an arm injury.

Daniels was a fourth-round pick in this year's draft after he played collegiately for Oklahoma State and Oklahoma.

The rookie entered Sunday's game with 22 tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass defended.

articles.title: Falcons rookie Kendal Daniels stretchered off the field and ruled out after helmet-to-knee tackle
articles.summary: Kendal Daniels did have movement in one of his hands as he left the field.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was stretchered off the field in Week 6 after his helmet made contact with Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland's knee on a tackle attempt.

Daniels laid down on the field for roughly 10 minutes while he was attended to by medical personnel. Eventually, a decision was made to bring out a cart and stretcher for Daniels. The injury occurred with a little over eight minutes left to play in the third quarter.

Shortly after leaving the field, Daniels was ruled out with a neck injury.

Daniels was able to move his left hand as he was leaving the field. It was later reported that he has movement in all extremities.

The 24-year-old Daniels was selected by the Falcons in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He's started every single game for the team so far, and has 22 tackles and one sack on the season.

Prior to leaving Sunday's contest, Daniels was credited with seven total tackles, which led the team at the time.

articles.title: Dallas Goedert gets pants pulled down for pass interference call to set up Eagles TD vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Is it pass interference if you get your pants pulled down before the ball arrives?
articles.body:
Is it pass interference if you get your pants pulled down before the ball arrives?

It's a question that actually came up during Sunday's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Carolina Panthers.

With the Eagles trailing 10-0 late in the first half, backup Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee targeted tight end Dallas Goedert on a deep pass into the end zone from the Carolina 25-yard line. Goedert flopped to the turf with what appeared at first glance like little to no contact from Panthers cornerback Will Lee and drew a flag.

The CBS broadcast team of Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker was perplexed at the call. But replay revealed some contact not seen on an initial look — and a bit more of Goedert than Goedert intended to show of himself on TV.

As Goedert broke toward the sideline on his route, Lee grabbed a hold of Goedert's pants and tugged them down just enough to expose Goedert's backside.

Tucker was in the midst of criticizing the call when replay revealed the minor wardrobe malfunction.

"What? They called that pass interference?" Tucker proclaimed as the pants tug was revealed. "I mean, if anything, I think it would be illegal contact on pulling his pants down before the ball was in the there."

Tucker may or may not have been right about the ball being in the air. It was a long pass from McKee, and it wasn't clear from the broadcast shot whether the ball was in the air when the pants tug took place.

It was also initially unclear if officials flagged pass interference for the pants tug or the ensuing flop job from Goedert as the ball arrived.

But they spotted the ball at the 3-yard line — close to where the pants tug took place — instead of at the 1-yard line for contact in the end zone, where Goedert flopped. It appears the pants tug was the culprit.

Two plays later, Dameon Pierce ran the ball in for a 2-yard touchdown to get the Eagles on the board. And Goedert, a fan favorite in Philadelphia, took one for the team in a manner that he surely didn't see coming.

In the end, the touchdown wasn't enough to spark the Eagles as the Panthers held on for a 25-14 win to send Philadelphia to 2-4 with a fourth straight loss. Carolina improved to 3-2 with the win.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Box Score Stats, Highlights After Jameis Winston Benched in Giants vs. Saints
articles.summary: With Jameis Winston struggling against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, the New York Giants turned to their backup quarterback.
articles.body:
With Jameis Winston struggling against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, the New York Giants turned to their backup quarterback.

J.J. McCarthy, whom the Giants acquired from the Minnesota Vikings earlier this month, came in for New York in the fourth quarter after Winston threw a pair of interceptions through the first three quarters.

McCarthy put together a solid day and nearly led the Giants to a comeback win.

McCarthy's first drive in a Giants' uniform didn't end well, as he threw an interception.

McCarthy turned things around after the interception, though, leading New York to back-to-back touchdown drives, plus a field goal to bring the Giants within a touchdown in the final minutes.

The Giants ultimately came up just short, but it was a promising debut for McCarthy.

Winston had put together a disappointing performance against his former team before coming out, throwing for 152 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions on 14-of-26 passing.

Last week, Winston had his best showing of the season when he recorded 326 yards and three touchdowns against the Washington Commanders. Clearly, he didn't carry his momentum into Week 6.

McCarthy, the 10th overall pick in 2024, is looking for a fresh start in New York after a rough start to his career. After missing all of his rookie year, he had 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 10 games last year.

After losing the quarterback battle to Kyler Murray in Minnesota, McCarthy was demoted to the third-string position. The move to the Giants gave him the chance for a higher position on the depth chart, and New York gave him his first opportunity just a few weeks after he was traded.

The question now is whether McCarthy or Winston will get the nod next week against the Houston Texans. The Giants are still technically alive in the playoff race, but few are expecting them to make a run without star quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Winston is the veteran of the group, but after the way McCarthy finished Sunday's game, it'd be hard not to put him under center next week.

articles.title: Bears' Jahdae Walker Ejected for Head Butting Falcons' Chris Blair
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears controlled the first three-plus quarters of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons, but it wasn't all good news for the NFC North team.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears controlled the first three-plus quarters of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons, but it wasn't all good news for the NFC North team.

ESPN's Courtney Cronin reported wide receiver Jahdae Walker was ejected early in the fourth quarter when he head butted Falcons wide receiver Chris Blair. The play happened on a kickoff with Chicago kicking the ball to Atlanta after going up 31-7 on a Cairo Santos field goal.

It was yet another penalty for the Bears.

Cronin noted it was their 12th for 133 yards, which was their most in a single game since the 2016 campaign. A number of them, including multiple holdings and an offensive pass interference on Colston Loveland, nullified big plays for the offense.

While Chicago thoroughly outplayed the Falcons for extended stretches leading up to Walker's ejection, the penalties were a problem and something for head coach Ben Johnson to focus on moving forward.

As for Walker, he's a secondary receiver in the aerial attack.

Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze, Kalif Raymond and tight end Colston Loveland are typically going to see more targets when the Bears drop back to throw, although Walker plays on special teams and scored a touchdown in the opener against the Carolina Panthers.

Walker entered Sunday's contest with just the one catch for one yard and a touchdown from that win over Carolina.

He had six catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns last season.

articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns overcame an early 10-point deficit to steal a 13-10 victory over the AFC North rival Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns overcame an early 10-point deficit to steal a 13-10 victory over the AFC North rival Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.

Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson engineered a 10-play, 62-yard drive to set up a game-winning 37-yard field goal by Andre Szmyt, who had benefited from a defensive offsides penalty when his first attempt was blocked. The win put Cleveland in a tie with Baltimore for first place in the AFC North at 4-2.

The Browns were understandably in a celebratory mood after the win:

The game was a grind that didn't have many big performances, but the top players are as follows:

While Watson and the rest of the Browns' passing attack struggled to find a rhythm for most of the game, he managed to connect with veteran wideout Jerry Jeudy late in the contest to help set up the game-winning field goal.

The Ravens were playing without star quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second straight game. While backup Tyler Huntley was solid with 165 yards and a touchdown, star running back Derrick Henry couldn't get much going on the ground. The five-time Pro Bowler lost his first fumble of the season in the fourth quarter.

The Browns will be riding high into their Week 7 meeting against the Tennessee Titans, while the Ravens will try to bounce back in another division matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Cam Ward, Titans Get 1st Win of Season as NFL Fans Troll Daniel Jones, Colts
articles.summary: At long last, Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans are victorious.
articles.body:
At long last, Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans are victorious.

Ward and the Titans beat the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 on Sunday after starting the season 0-5. While it wasn't a banner day for Ward, he nonetheless managed to get the win against a divisional foe.

What helped the Titans get the win was a rough day from Daniel Jones, who had a pair of interceptions. Fans trolled the Colts' quarterback on social media afterwards.

Jones finished Sunday's loss with 269 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. The Colts trailed by three points with just over two minutes to go, but Jones and the offense turned it over on downs after just five plays.

After the Titans went up 26-20, Indianapolis' final attempt to take the lead ended with it turning it over on downs once again.

The win for the Titans came despite Ward throwing for just 102 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

Jones had a career year in his first season with the Colts in 2025, but he hasn't been the same player this year. Through six games, he's thrown for 1,290 yards, four touchdowns and six interceptions.

Indianapolis is 2-4 after the loss to the Titans on Sunday, with its playoff hopes quickly dwindling.

"We've got a lot to fix, and we've got to fix it in a hurry," Colts' head coach Shane Steichen told reporters after the loss.

Brock Bowers finished the first half without a catch, but his teammate Michael Mayer led the Raiders in receptions with 5 for 52 yards.

The Bills and Raiders are tied 13-13 at halftime.

Quarterbacks Josh Allen and Kirk Cousins are having a great duel. Allen is 12-of-16 for 144 yards passing and a touchdown. While, Cousins is 12-of-17 for 126 yards.

Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was ejected just before halftime. This was not a smart decision by CGJ; now his day is over.

Kwity Paye and Maxx Crosby had a scheduled meeting at the QB.

Josh Palmer had a bad drop on the last drive. Buffalo fans can't wait for DJ Moore to be fully healthy again.

Going with a Conner Hayward tush push while having Brock Bowers is a CHOICE. Bowers is close to finishing the first half with a goose egg on the stat sheet. WOW!

A slot screen to Khalil Shakir, and he does the rest for the touchdown. Rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell (#13) makes a great block, springing Shakir.

Hezekiah Masses is now in the Raiders' defensive lineup. The rookie cornerback has been a bright spot early in his career.

Blocking Maxx Crosby should come with hazard pay!

Great pass breakup by rookie defensive back Treydan Stukes.

Joe Brady is making a conscious effort to get Dalton Kincaid going early today.

Ashton Jeanty caps off a strong opening series for the Raiders with a touchdown.

The Raiders didn't get off the field on their first 3rd-down attempt, but this time they brought down Josh Allen for a sack. The Bills lead 3-0 early.

You don't see this every Sunday in the NFL.

The Raiders make an interesting choice by starting Darien Porter over emerging rookie CB Hezekiah Masses, who leads the team in passes defended and interceptions.

articles.title: Bears Beat Falcons, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Caleb Williams, Penix, Bijan, Top Players
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears defeated the Atlanta Falcons with a 31-23 on Sunday in Caleb Williams' first game back since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears defeated the Atlanta Falcons with a 31-23 on Sunday in Caleb Williams' first game back since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2.

The Bears were 1.5-point favorites over the Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

They exceeded expectations before Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons attempted a fourth-quarter comeback, scoring 16 unanswered points.

Williams stepped in his return, converting 9-of-17 third downs in the win after being sidelined for three games. He looked to be in good shape Sunday, finishing with 305 yards, completing 83 percent of his passes.

Chicago scored on both of its first-quarter possessions while holding Atlanta to one three-and-out.

Williams connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 14-yard pass before D'Andre Swift rushed for a 4-yard touchdown, giving the Bears a 14-0 lead after the first quarter.

Despite a missed 56-yard field goal, Chicago maintained its lead into halftime, 21-7, holding Atlanta to one touchdown as Penix Jr. found Jahan Dotson for a score.

A muffed punt by Atlanta's Zachariah Branch was recovered at the Falcons' 10-yard line, and the Bears turned a three-play drive into Swift's second touchdown of the day before halftime.

Chicago added another rushing touchdown out of halftime, with Roschon Johnson finding the end zone as Atlanta's struggles continued.

The Falcons turned the ball over on downs before Branch fumbled another punt, closing out the third quarter trailing 28-7.

Atlanta found its rhythm in the fourth quarter, scoring 16 straight points to make it a one-score game.

Kyle Pitts Sr. caught a pass from Penix before finding Branch for the two-point conversion. A Chicago fumble then led to another Falcons touchdown, with Penix Jr. and Pitts Sr. running it back. Penix Jr. found Drake London for another successful two-point conversion.

The Falcons had a chance to march down the field and tie the game after retaking possession with under four minutes remaining, but Penix Jr. was sacked and fumbled, effectively ending the game.

The Bears will be back in action Thursday when they host the New England Patriots, while Atlanta will host the San Francisco 49ers next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: New Rams Kicker Blake Grupe Injured in 1st Game Since Replacing 'Thiccer Kicker' Harrison Mevis
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams have a kicker problem.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have a kicker problem.

Blake Grupe—who was signed this week to replace Harrison Mevis—suffered a knee injury during Sunday's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals while covering a kick-off:

Mevis was just 5-for-9 on field goals this season, which included a miss and blocked attempt during last week's 37-34 overtime loss against the Buffalo Bills. His release didn't come as a major surprise.

Special teams have been an issue for the Rams in general—last season, head coach Sean McVay fired special-teams coordinator Chase Blackburn late in the season after gaffes from that unit contributed to a number of losses.

"This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of," McVay said of his special teams' group this season. "We'll lean in. We'll go back to work. We'll use these as growth opportunities."

Grupe, 27, was expected to upgrade the kicker position. He started his career with the New Orleans Saints (2023-25) before a five-game stint with the Indianapolis Colts last season, where he was 11-for-11 on field goals and 10-for-10 on extra points. For his career he's 86-for-105 on field goals.

"Those five weeks in Indy were seriously big for me, big for my career," he told reporters this past week. "I was able to get the ball rolling and show what I can do, and that was big for me."

But the Colts gave the starting kicker position back to the previously injured Spencer Shrader over the summer and released Grupe, who then picked up with the New York Jets on their practice squad before the Rams signed him this week.

Unfortunately for both Grupe and the Rams, injury very quickly struck. It had an immediate impact on Sunday—after scoring their first touchdown, the team went for a two-point try instead of kicking and failed to convert.

articles.title: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy misses halftime of OT win over Buccaneers, visits medical tent for treatment for ankle injury
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy never made it to the locker room at halftime.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy wasn't able to address his team as usual at halftime on Sunday in their overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

On his way to his halftime interview at Raymond James Stadium, McCarthy apparently injured his ankle.

Broadcast cameras did not appear to catch the injury on video. Instead, McCarthy was shown having trouble as he tried to walk off the field at halftime. He eventually decided to head straight into the blue medical tent on the sideline, where he remained for all of halftime. He never made it back to the locker room to address the Steelers, and re-joined the team at the start of the third quarter.

Despite the injury, McCarthy continued coaching the team in the second half normally. His ankle injury appeared to be minor after all.

And, despite falling into a 13-point hole in the fourth quarter, Aaron Rodgers led the Steelers storming back to force overtime . He eventually found Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown pass in the extra period, too. The score was the first of Bernard's career, and lifted the Steelers to a second straight win.

Rodgers went 33-of-49 passing for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the win, which moved the Steelers to 4-2 on the season. They are in a great spot in the AFC North race, but the win in Tampa was much more complicated than it needed to be. Rodgers could have sealed the win in regulation, but couldn't find the end zone from the 3-yard line after Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels threw his second interception of the fourth quarter.

But a win is a win, and McCarthy's halftime injury didn't appear to hinder him much in the end. He and the Steelers can head home happy.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Praised by Giants' Harbaugh After Replacing Jameis Winston, Week 7 Starter TBD
articles.summary: The New York Giants aren't ready to name J.J. McCarthy the starting quarterback going forward after he replaced Jameis Winston during Sunday's 34-27 loss against the New Orleans Saints and played well.
articles.body:
The New York Giants aren't ready to name J.J. McCarthy the starting quarterback going forward after he replaced Jameis Winston during Sunday's 34-27 loss against the New Orleans Saints and played well.

But head coach John Harbaugh liked what he saw.

"I thought he came in there and did a heck of a job given the circumstances," he told reporters. "Kinda desperation time, I mean it's different from normal football. But he made some plays and gave us a chance at the end to win the game, ended up throwing the ball into the end zone at the end so that was good."

McCarthy discussed his performance after the game:

McCarthy replaced Winston in the fourth quarter after the veteran starter threw his second interception of the game (he also took four sacks). The Giants trailed 34-10 at the time.

The substitution didn't pay immediate dividends—McCarthy threw a pick of his own. But he promptly led three straight scoring drives, cutting the deficit to 34-27, and the Giants got the ball back with about a minute remaining in the game and the chance to tie it. A 28-yard run from the quarterback and a pair of completions for 29 yards drove the Giants down to the New Orleans' 14 with 13 seconds remaining. A fourth-and-one incompletion ultimately sealed the loss, but not before McCarthy gave the team some life.

Overall he finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception, taking a sack. He also rushed twice for 26 yards. Not too shabby for playing one quarter.

Given the topsy-turvy play of Winston, a trend throughout his career, the Giants very well may have a quarterback controversy on their hands. Winston has now thrown for two interceptions and taken four sacks in two of his last three starts, and with the NFC East wide open this year, the Giants have an opportunity they cannot afford to squander.

It's about to be a very interesting week in New York, in other words.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Didn't Have 'Best Effort' with Career-High Drops in Injury Return, Patriots' Vrabel Says
articles.summary: In his first game since Week 1, A.J. Brown had just three receptions for 27 yards and dropped a career-high three passes as the New England Patriots beat the New York Jets.
articles.body:
In his first game since Week 1, A.J. Brown had just three receptions for 27 yards and dropped a career-high three passes as the New England Patriots beat the New York Jets.

After the game, head coach Mike Vrabel said the veteran receiver didn't have his "best effort" in the game.

"Unfortunately, it wasn't his best effort," Vrabel said. "I know that, he knows that. We have all the confidence in the world in A.J. to finish the plays."

Brown was targeted 10 times in Sunday's game, so quarterback Drake Maye gave him plenty of opportunities to make something happen, but it ultimately wasn't his day.

Brown even failed to recover an onside kick, though his teammates bailed him out of what could've been a costly mistake.

Brown, who was traded to the Patriots from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks and landed on the injury reserve. While he's been out for the last four games, he said his ankle injury isn't an excuse for his performance on Sunday.

"There's no excuses. I stacked my guy, should've made the play. I beat my guy on third down, should've made the play," Brown told reporters . "So, ankle or not, gotta make all those plays."

Brown figures to be one of Maye's top targets this year, but the Patriots can't afford more drops as they try to get back to the Super Bowl.

New England has a short week and will face the Chicago Bears on Thursday, and Brown is looking to turn things around when he takes the field next.

"Just tryna get going again, best foot forward, put this to be really fast," Brown said. "I'm gonna watch the tape. It's over. I'm gonna flush it."

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Says He Was 'Punished' for Fumbles, Giants' John Harbaugh Explains RB's 0 Carries
articles.summary: After his recent struggles to hold onto the football, Cam Skattebo saw his production take a major hit against the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body:
After his recent struggles to hold onto the football, Cam Skattebo saw his production take a major hit against the New Orleans Saints.

The New York Giants running back had no carries in the loss and said he was "punished" for his mistake from last week.

Head coach John Harbaugh had a different perspective, saying Skattebo's lack of playing time wasn't a benching.

"It was not by design," Harbaugh said. "I mean, all those guys were taking equal reps in the first half. We were trying to see who could make something happen, who could kinda get a hot hand and earn it. Nobody's really taking the bull by the horns... It wasn't by design for him not to carry the ball. It was just, when he was in there, we didn't call any runs."

Skattebo has had a decent start to his second NFL season, but fumbles have been a persistent issue. He's fumbled four times through the first six games, including a costly one last week.

The Giants were in overtime with the Washington Commanders and had the ball in field goal range when Skattebo fumbled and cost New York a chance to win the game. The game instead ended in a tie.

While Skattebo didn't see any action on Sunday, the Giants didn't turn to the run game much in the loss. Tyrone Tracy Jr. led the way with six carries and Devin Singletary and Najee Harris each had just one as well.

New York had just 84 total rushing yards on 20 carries in the game.

Harbaugh added that Skattebo's six snaps were a result of splitting reps between so many players, and he said he's hoping someone will assert themselves as the true RB1.

"You're balancing it between four guys," Harbaugh told reporters . "Do the math: how many plays were there? That was our plan. You can argue that, you can say, 'Well, I don't like that. I don't like you dividing up the snaps between four backs.' Hey, I don't like it either. One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. None of those guys have done that yet. And when one of those guys steps up to be the back, then they'll be the back. There's your answer."

The Giants' run game has been a flawed area to start the season, and clearly Harbaugh is searching for answers after dropping to 3-2-1.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers rally for OT win in Tampa as Buccaneers' struggles continue without Baker Mayfield
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers need Baker Mayfield back on the field.

The Buccaneers blew a 13-point lead in the fourth quarter and allowed Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers to rally and take the 26-19 win in overtime at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. That dropped the Buccaneers to 1-5, and a brutal 0-4 on their home field.

Rodgers and the Steelers, who had a look to end the game in regulation, mounted a long drive in overtime that he capped with a six-yard pass to Germie Bernard for the touchdown. That was Barnard's first career touchdown, too, and eventually gave them the win.

Jalon Daniels, who stepped in to replace Mayfield in Week 4 , threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter on Sunday. While Daniels guided the team to their first win of the season last week in Dallas, he's now just 1-2 in the first three starts of his career. And the Buccaneers are now almost certainly out of reach of the postseason.

Mayfield went down in the team's loss to the Minnesota Vikings last month after he dislocated his right thumb while throwing an interception. An MRI later revealed no ligament damage, but Mayfield has not played since and could be out as many as six weeks .

Daniels got the start the following week, and couldn't quite lead the Buccaneers past the Green Bay Packers. He threw two interceptions in that outing, which was his first NFL. But last week, Daniels and the Buccaneers rolled to a win over the Dallas Cowboys behind a huge night from Bucky Irving.

At least briefly on Sunday, it looked like Daniels and the Buccaneers were going to pick up right where they left off. They took a 13-3 lead into the locker room at halftime, and Daniels found Emeka Egbuka for a two-yard touchdown early on. But after pushing that lead to 13 points after a Chase McLaughlin field goal in the third quarter, Rodgers and the Steelers started mounting their comeback.

Rodgers led the Steelers on their first touchdown drive of the day early in the fourth quarter, and found a wide-open Darnell Washington for the score to make it a one-score contest.

Then just three plays later, Daniels threw a bad interception right to Daylen Everette. Daniels just threw it up there on third down, which led to an easy field goal for Chris Boswell. That was the 310th made field goal of his career, too, which is the most in team history.

The Steelers' defense shut Daniels down again after that, and forced a quick punt in less than a minute. Rodgers put the Steelers in scoring position at the two-minute warning, but he took a huge sack on third down to force them to take another field goal. That tied the game up 16-16.

Any momentum that Daniels had offensively was long gone by this point. On just his second play after the Boswell field goal, he threw what nearly turned into a pick-six. While looking for Egbuka, Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean jumped the pass and ran it down to the 3-yard line.

Somehow, Rodgers couldn't punch it in from there. The 20-yard chip shot that put them ahead only lasted briefly. Daniels completed his first pass after missing nine straight, and found Ted Hurst for a 22-yard gain to quickly get them into position to drill a 53-yarder to force overtime.

But that led to Rodgers' game-winning drive, and the Steelers' final stop to seal their seven-point win. Rodgers went 33-of-49 for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The Steelers now sit at 4-2. While they are still in great position in the AFC North, the win was much more complicated than it needed to be. They were on the 3-yard line in the fourth quarter, after all, and had to settle for a field goal instead of a game-winning touchdown.

Daniels went 22-of-43 for 164 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He won't keep the starting job in Tampa for much longer. The reins will be handed back over to Mayfield as soon as he's able to get back onto the field. While Daniels did lead the team to their first win of the season, the Buccaneers are undoubtedly missing Mayfield.

Though a playoff push isn't completely out of the question — the San Diego Chargers lost four straight in 1992 and still made the postseason, though they are the only team in NFL history to accomplish that feat — it's going to take a massive turnaround to pull that off. And that'll have to happen quickly.

articles.title: NFL Week 6 Winners and Losers: With another listless loss, Eagles face possibility of major changes
articles.summary: The Eagles' season is quickly slipping away.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles looked like a potential dynasty 20 months ago.

They blasted Kansas City in Super Bowl LIX, delivering a big blow to the Chiefs' dynasty. The Eagles were a dominant champion, winning 16 of their last 17 games in that title run. Their roster was considered the best in the NFL and it wasn't even a debate. The Eagles were going to be a force for many years to come.

Less than two calendar years later, it's worth asking if the Eagles need to start a rebuild.

The current state of the Eagles is that they're one of the NFL's most unimpressive teams and the future is not as bright as everyone thought. With Jalen Hurts out due to a blood clot , Tanner McKee started and didn't do much in a 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers . McKee had just 215 yards on 45 attempts.

Philadelphia's defense tried to keep the Eagles in the game but ultimately gave up 401 yards and 25 points. The Eagles are 2-4. Their only wins were close calls against the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans, who have combined for two victories this season. Philadelphia has lost four in a row since, and the cracks are everywhere.

The injuries are the biggest problem, but that's only part of the story. A roster that looked impeccable during that Super Bowl run is decaying rapidly. The offensive line is a shell of what it was, and losing right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement leaves a big hole. The receiving corps is mediocre without A.J. Brown. Saquon Barkley has been hurt but his numbers have fallen off since his incredible (and high volume) 2024 season and he's 29 years old. The defense is fine but far from dominant. A trade by general manager Howie Roseman, sending two third-round draft picks for Jonathan Greenard after miscalculating the market on Jaelan Phillips in free agency, has been terrible since Greenard has been mostly injured. Greenard had one tackle this season before Sunday's game and didn't record a stat against the Panthers.

Everything has to be on the table for the Eagles, who don't know when Hurts will be coming off injured reserve. They could and probably should be major sellers at the trade deadline, and maybe even some stars like Barkley could be moved if the salary cap ramifications can be figured out.

Head coach Nick Sirianni has to be on the hot seat after last season's disappointment and this season's terrible start. Even the future of Hurts, who hasn't played anywhere near an elite level after winning Super Bowl MVP, has to be at least discussed even though preseason hero McKee clearly isn't the in-house answer. Hurts isn't playing to the level of the five-year, $255 million deal he signed in 2023 and that has to get fixed. Changing offensive coordinators this past offseason didn't work.

There are no signs the Eagles are even a decent team this season. There are talented pieces to build around but the overall health of the roster is a concern. The coaching staff is going to be under fire the rest of the season if it doesn't get better, and it probably won't with McKee or whoever else the Eagles play at quarterback in Hurts' absence. It will be hard to redo the roster and possibly the coaching staff so soon after a dominant Super Bowl season, but it might already be time for it in Philadelphia.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 6 of the NFL season:

Tennessee Titans, winless no more: The Titans looked like they were headed toward 0-6 when Cam Ward had a bad first half and they trailed 13-0 at halftime in Indianapolis.

But the Titans rallied as the Colts fell apart. A blocked punt that was scooped up for a touchdown gave the Titans the lead in the fourth quarter, and even after the Colts answered to tie it, the Titans put together a drive for a go-ahead field goal. Their defense got two stops after that, including one on a Hail Mary on the final play, and they held on to a 26-20 win.

It has been a rough few seasons for the Titans, and a bad start to this season. But they got a win. And all the questions about how long it might take for them to collect their first win are over.

Jerry Jeudy and the first-place Browns: Jeudy has been mostly a forgotten man for the Cleveland Browns, with an influx of young receiving talent. But he made the biggest play of Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens .

With the game tied 10-10 and less than a minute to go, Jeudy got open in the middle of the field and gained 33 yards to the Ravens' 29-yard line. Andre Szmyt hit the game-winner as time expired and the Browns had a 13-10 win.

Jeudy had just eight catches for 81 yards this season before Sunday, but had four grabs for 69 yards against the Ravens, including the play that led to the win.

The Browns keep collecting wins in the final minutes, and find themselves 4-2. That puts them in first place for the moment since they have the tiebreaker over the 4-2 Steelers and Ravens, who had little offensive punch without Lamar Jackson (ankle) on Sunday.

It will be hard for the Browns to maintain this pace because close wins like they've had aren't guaranteed to continue. But it's a great start to the season in Cleveland.

Drake Maye: Remember when Maye was in a slump to start the season? That's over.

Maye threw three more touchdowns with no interceptions and the New England Patriots beat the New York Jets 26-19 to improve to 4-2. Maye has 10 passing touchdowns the past three weeks as the Patriots have gone from a very early season disappointment to one of the hottest teams in the NFL.

A.J. Brown had a quiet return to the lineup with 27 receiving yards and some drops , but just having him back is a boost to a New England offense that had already started to gain momentum.

Maye was criticized heavily for his start, which came after a poor postseason. But he's back to his near-MVP level the past few weeks.

DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard: The Pittsburgh Steelers were terrible for three quarters against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. But they rallied, with Aaron Rodgers hitting his top two receivers over and over again.

Metcalf had 11 catches for 93 yards, including a huge 16-yard gain on third-and-13 to start overtime. Bernard, a rookie, also had 11 catches for 87 yards and he scored the go-ahead touchdown in overtime. The Steelers got a stop after that on a fourth-down sack by Jalen Ramsey, who had a huge game with four tackles for loss and two sacks, and Pittsburgh had a 26-19 win after trailing 16-3 to start the fourth quarter.

Bernard, a second-round draft pick, had 80 yards last week and is emerging as a trusted target for Rodgers. Metcalf is the Steelers' most talented receiver and that showed Sunday.

The Steelers are 4-2 and while they're flawed, perhaps the passing game will continue to get better with those top two receivers playing well.

C.J. Stroud: When the Houston Texans were 0-4 and Stroud wasn't playing well without Nico Collins, a lot of questions were starting to pile up about what Houston would do with its quarterback in terms of a long-term extension.

Stroud and the Texans are turning around those questions. They've won two straight after a thrilling 34-31 victory in London over the Jacksonville Jaguars . They're two games behind Jacksonville in the division, but they're alive.

Stroud played one of his best games since his rookie season. He had 312 yards and three touchdowns and completed a couple of passes to help Houston get in field-goal range for Ka'imi Fairbairn, who hit a 49-yarder as time expired to win it.

Stroud was hot all game against a good Jaguars defense. A lot has changed with him and his team in two weeks.

Jameis Winston: The clock is going to run out on Winston and the New York Giants, who entered Sunday a fluky 3-1-1.

Winston will be blamed for the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints . When Winston threw a bad interception over the middle, which led to a Saints touchdown and a 34-10 deficit, it was time to pull Winston.

J.J. McCarthy came in and threw an interception right away, but he also led the Giants to 17 fourth-quarter points. The Giants had the ball in the final minute with a chance to at least tie it. But McCarthy threw incomplete on fourth down in the final seconds in the defeat. McCarthy threw for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter.

After Sunday, it would be a surprise if McCarthy doesn't start for the Giants in Week 7 at the Houston Texans.

The Giants are still in first place, but that's because the NFC East is the worst division in the NFL so far this season. Winston's inconsistency has always been extreme, and while he has some good moments he also plays like he did Sunday when he had 152 yards and two interceptions before being benched.

The Giants don't have a great quarterback option to save their season with Jaxson Dart done for the year, but McCarthy's performance Sunday was interesting. It's probably enough to earn him the Giants' next start.

Atlanta Falcons' hot streak: We'll fondly recall those two weeks when the Falcons looked like a reborn team with Michael Penix Jr. returning at quarterback.

Atlanta doesn't look like much of a threat anymore. Sure, the Falcons rallied to make it interesting in the fourth quarter, after a bad start, but Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon got his third sack of the game, causing a fumble that Chicago recovered, when Atlanta had the ball down only eight points in the fourth quarter. That put the finishing touches on a 31-23 Bears win .

A big turning point came late in the first half when rookie Zachariah Branch muffed a punt on his own 10-yard line late in the first half. The Bears scored right after that to take a 21-7 lead into halftime. Branch would lose a fumble in the second half too.

While there were signs of life against Chicago, after the Bears let up with a 31-7 lead, the overall performance wasn't nearly good enough. Atlanta's defense was picked apart for three quarters and its offense did little to answer until the fourth quarter.

The Falcons are 2-4 after Sunday. They're not the threat they looked like for a couple weeks.

articles.title: Bills' CJGJ Ejected for Spitting in Direction of Brock Bowers, Raiders Players in Trending Video
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter after appearing to spit in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Las Vegas Raiders players.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter after appearing to spit in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Las Vegas Raiders players.

Gardner-Johnson, 28, is never far from controversy, so Sunday's ejection won't shock anybody. But it left the Bills without a defensive starter for the entire second half.

The NFL could decide to take further disciplinary action against Gardner-Johnson upon further review next week.

Last season, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was ejected before the first play of the team's season opener against the Dallas Cowboys for spitting in the direction of Dak Prescott.

The league ultimately ruled that because Carter did not play a down, he served his one-game suspension in Week 1 and was therefore eligible to play in Week 2.

articles.title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe knocks himself out of his debut with a disastrous tackle attempt
articles.summary: Blake Grupe nailed a 44-yard field goal on his first drive as the new Los Angeles Rams kicker, then injured his knee on the very next kickoff.
articles.body: Within a week, the Los Angeles Rams waived a kicker for blowing an overtime game-winner against Buffalo, signed Blake Grupe as his replacement, watched Grupe hit a 44-yarder on his first drive, and then lost him to a self-inflicted knee injury on the very next play. Grupe initially delivered on Sunday, capping the offense's opening drive with a successful 44-yard field goal. That momentum vanished seconds later on the ensuing kickoff. Grupe was the last line of defense as Arizona Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay broke through the coverage, and the 5-foot-7 kicker aggressively lowered his shoulder to force Duvernay out of bounds at the 47-yard line. The collision left Grupe on all fours, grimacing in pain. Trainers took Grupe to the blue medical tent before he retreated to the locker room with a knee injury designation. He was ruled doubtful to return. articles.title: Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson ejected for spitting at Raiders tight end Brock Bowers
articles.summary: A an official saw the incident on the field and immediately ejected Gardner-Johnson.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected on Sunday for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

The incident took place late in the second quarter. Gardner-Johnson and Bowers exchanged words in between plays. A game official intervened and quickly threw a flag and announced Gardner-Johnson's ejection.

It wasn't immediately clear on the game broadcast what prompted the ejection. But slow-motion replay showed that Gardner-Johnson spit at Bowers as Bowers had his back turned.

The Bills held a 13-10 lead at the time of the incident. The unsportsmanlike conduct penalty moved the Raiders from Buffalo's 29-yard line to the 14 with 15 seconds remaining before halftime. Las Vegas ended up kicking a field goal before halftime to tie the game at 13-13.

The ejection is the second of Gardner-Johnson's NFL career. He was previously tossed from a 2024 game against the Washington Commanders while playing for the Philadelphia Eagles.

In that instance, Gardner-Johnson got called for his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for taunting, leading to his automatic Johnson. As he left the field, he flipped off the Washington crowd with both hands.

The spitting incident is the second in the NFL since last season that led to an ejection. In the 2025 season opener between the Eagles and Cowboys, Philadelphia defensive lineman Jalen Carter spit on Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott before the first snap of the game.

Carter was ejected without playing a down. He was not, however, suspended. The NFL fined Carter $57,222 for the incident , and his ejection from the Cowboys game before it started reportedly served as a one-game suspension in the NFL's eyes.

The NFL will certainly take another look at Gardner-Johnson's incident, and a suspension could be on the table for the Buffalo safety.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy throws first touchdown pass for Giants, nearly leads game-tying comeback
articles.summary: McCarthy entered the game with the Giants trailing 34-10 and led two touchdown drives.
articles.body:
Making his second appearance for the New York Giants since being traded from the Minnesota Vikings , quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw his first touchdown pass for his new team during Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints.

With 5:04 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Giants trailing 34-18, McCarthy finished off a three-play, 78-yard drive by hitting tight end Isaiah Likely down the left hash on a seam route for a 24-yard score.

The third-year QB entered the game with 11:25 left in the fourth and the Giants facing a 34-10 deficit. He replaced Jameis Winston, who threw an interception on New York's previous possession. The Saints took over at New York's 21-yard line and scored in two plays, capped by Tyler Shough connecting with Chris Olave for an 18-yard touchdown.

McCarthy's first series ended with an interception. On the fifth play of the series, facing a third-and-10 from the Saints' 44-yard line, McCarthy looked for Malachi Fields on a short drag route but was picked off by Martin Emerson Jr.

But the Giants got the ball back two plays later when safety Jason Pinnock forced a fumble by running back C.J. Donaldson. New York took over at its 48-yard line and took six plays to find the end zone on a 5-yard run by Tyrone Tracy Jr. McCarthy connected with Likely on a 2-point conversion to pull the Giants to within two scores.

New York then forced a three-and-out by New Orleans and took over on offense with 5:54 left in regulation. McCarthy hit Charlie Jones for a 49-yard pass, then followed an incompletion with his scoring throw to Likely that cut the Saints' lead to 10 points.

After the defense forced another three-and-out, the Giants followed up with a 7-yard, 69-yard drive that ended with a 41-yard Dominic Zvada field goal to pull New York to within one touchdown.

The Giants had an opportunity to tie the score (or take the lead) with 0:57 remaining. But they used their final two timeouts on the previous defensive series. That likely factored into McCarthy's decision-making process on New York's final offensive play.

McCarthy opened the drive with a 28-yard run and connected with Likely on a 20-yard gain, alternating with two spikes to stop the clock. He then hit Malik Nabers for a 9-yard pass, followed by a spike to stop the clock with 12 seconds remaining.

On the Giants' final play, McCarthy appeared to have Nabers open for a touchdown under the goal posts but made the wrong read. He also probably could have run to the right for a first down on fourth-and-1. But with no timeouts left, the clock likely would have expired.

After making no throws in a brief appearance in last week's overtime tie with the Washington Commanders, McCarthy finished with 243 yards passing — in under 12 minutes — while completing 11 of 21 passes for 1 touchdown and 1 interception. He also ran for 26 yards on 2 rushes.

The question might now become whether that performance was enough for head coach John Harbaugh to consider giving McCarthy the start next week at the Houston Texans.

articles.title: 'Special' Travis Hunter Hyped by Trevor Lawrence After Historic Game, HC Says It's Part of 'Plan'
articles.summary: Despite Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in the NFL London Game at Wembley Stadium, the Jacksonville Jaguars couldn't help but be excited by Travis Hunter's historic performance.
articles.body:
Despite Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in the NFL London Game at Wembley Stadium, the Jacksonville Jaguars couldn't help but be excited by Travis Hunter's historic performance.

Hunter caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and produced three tackles and an interception in Sunday's loss. The 23-year-old is now the fifth player in the Super Bowl era, including the playoffs, with a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game, and the first to do so since Philadelphia Eagles star Brian Dawkins in 2002.

"Travis played awesome, made some huge plays for us, gave us a spark," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said after the game, per Ken Maguire of the Associated Press. "It was cool to get him involved. He's special with the ball in his hands."

Head coach Liam Coen revealed that the Jags planned to get Hunter more involved on offense this week after he spent most of the 2026 season focusing on his defensive duties as a starting cornerback. He could see more time on offense going forward.

"That was part of the plan, getting him a little bit more involved early, made some critical plays for us on both sides of the football obviously," Coen said. "I was proud of the way he competed, made some plays for us on offense. Got to keep building off of it."

Hunter will try to keep working on his two-way skills during the bye week before the Jags (4-2) return to action on Nov. 1 against the Indianapolis Colts (2-4).

articles.title: Rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., returning from injury, a silver lining in Jets' loss to Patriots
articles.summary: Despite missing the last four weeks due to an ankle injury, rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets in receiving yards in their Week 6 loss to the...
articles.body:
The Jets slipped back into the loss column Sunday, falling just one touchdown behind AFC East-rival New England Patriots behind a series of missed opportunities and costly mistakes by the O-line.

But one silver lining may be found in rookie Omar Cooper Jr. , who made quite a statement as he took the field for the first time in over a month.

The 22-year-old wideout has been on IR since Week 1, when he sustained a high ankle sprain in the process of recording a 30-yard catch-and-run for his first NFL reception. He returned to the Jets lineup Sunday, leading all players — on both teams — in receiving yards (103) for his first career 100-yard game. Garrett Wilson 's 44 were the second-highest on the Jets.

"It was a great feeling," Cooper said after the game. "It felt good to finally be back out there."

Cooper, drafted 30th overall in this summer's NFL Draft, caught six of his seven targets Sunday, including a 48-yard pass that resulted in New York's first touchdown of the day. He almost recorded his first NFL touchdown on the Jets' opening drive, but it was waved off after an offensive pass interference call on Tim Patrick.

Though he's played less than two full games so far, he already seems to be someone quarterback Geno Smith can rely on.

"I think Omar did a tremendous job at coming back from injury," Smith said. "He fought just to get back out there, and what he did was showcase who he is: He's a playmaker. He's a guy who finds ways to make catches. The tough catches — he makes them look easy. Really impressed with the way that he performed, and looking forward to building on that."

Running back Braelon Allen agreed, noting that even though the Jets need "to stop playing against the Jets," Cooper was a bright spot on the teams's offense.

"He's shown flashes [of his ability], obviously, the one catch that he had the first week," Allen said. "Battled his way back and made some big plays for us today."

articles.title: NFL: Steelers-Saints game in Paris still on despite civil unrest
articles.summary: The game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints remains scheduled as planned despite civil unrest in the French capital, the NFL sai...
articles.body:
The game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints remains scheduled as planned despite civil unrest in the French capital, the NFL said Sunday.

The teams are set to play next Sunday at Stade de France in what would be the NFL's first regular-season game in Paris, where events are also planned for football fans during the week.

Rioting and looting have taken place during nationwide protests against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools .

"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the league said in a statement Sunday.

"We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."

The Saints were scheduled to arrive in Paris early Monday. The Steelers travel later in the week.

Hundreds of protesters gathered again on Sunday at the Place de la République amid a heavy police presence. Officers used tear gas as tensions flared sporadically in the neighborhood.

Dislodged cobblestones and broken glass littered the area. Looting and damage were also reported in other tourist and shopping districts.

Paris police said 855 people were arrested in the capital region.

French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday voiced the public's "anger" and "shame" over the rioting and looting.

articles.title: Patriots’ A.J. Brown Addresses Struggles in Return From Injury: ‘There’s No Excuses’
articles.summary: A.J. Brown has a plan to get back to form and prove his performance against the Jets was a one-time occurrence.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown will be the first to tell you he didn't have the best return to the field. He actually did so after the Patriots ' win against the Jets.

The receiver returned in Week 6 after an ankle injury he suffered in Week 1 sent him to IR. Brown caught three passes for 27 yards. He dropped three pass attempts for the first time in his career.

Brown also missed a catch during an onside kick attempt. Coach Mike Vrabel, Drake Maye, and others weren't concerned and supported Brown . Brown understands there may have been rust, but didn't mention that as the reason for his off game.

"There's no excuses," Brown said after the game via CLNS Media . "I stacked by guy, should've made the play. I beat my guy on third down, should've made the play. Ankle or not, I make all those plays."

A second-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft, Brown was traded from the Eagles to the Patriots for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick. He reunited with Vrabel after the two were together with the Titans.

Brown, with 1,003 receiving yards last season, will need to regroup quickly, as the Patriots face the Bears on Thursday night. He has a plan to get back to form and prove his performance against the Jets was a one-time occurrence.

"Short week. Just trying to just get going again… best foot forward. Put this to bed really fast. I'm going to watch the tape, and it's over, I'm going to flush it," Brown said.

articles.title: 'I got punished': Giants' Cam Skattebo goes without a touch in loss to Saints, one week after critical OT fumble
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo has four fumbles in five games this season.
articles.body:
Coming into Week 6, Cam Skattebo started every game for the New York Giants this season. But ahead of Sunday's game, reports started swirling that Najee Harris would take over as the team's starter due to Skattebo's fumbling issues.

Turns out, Harris wasn't the only member of the Giants to jump Skattebo on the depth chart. As the first half ended, Skattebo did not have a single touch against the New Orleans Saints.

He didn't get a touch in the second half either as the Giants lost 34-27 to the visiting New Orleans Saints.

"I got punished for what I did. I understand it, so I gotta be ready when coach calls my name and that wasn't today," Skattebo told The Athletic's Charlotte Carroll .

Three other Giant running backs were credited with a rushing attempt in the first quarter, a sign of what was in store for Skattebo on Sunday. In addition to Harris, who started the contest, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary all got rushing attempts in the first quarter.

Skattebo saw the field during the half, though far less than usual. He played just six snaps, never touching the ball.

Head coach John Harbaugh insisted that it wasn't a benching of Skattebo, he told reporters postgame.

"We were trying to see who could make something happen, who could get a hot hand," Harbaugh said of his running backs. "Nobody has really taken the bull by the horns."

Coming into the game, Skattebo had four fumbles in five games. The running back had not lost a fumble until Week 5, when he gave the ball up in overtime against the Washington Commanders.

The turnover put Washington in position to win the game, but the Giants were bailed out after the Commanders allowed time to expire in overtime without a field-goal attempt, resulting in a tie.

Fumbling wasn't a major issue for Skattebo as a rookie. In 101 attempts last season, the running back was credited with just one fumble. This season, he has four in 81 attempts.

articles.title: Jim Nantz Jokes 'My Wrist Is Broken' After Attempting 'Peanut Punch' with JJ Watt in Viral Video

articles.body:
Jim Nantz attempted a peanut punch on JJ Watt as the former NFL defensive lineman demonstrated how running backs are trying to protect the football this season during the broadcast of the Buffalo Bills vs. Las Vegas Raiders.

"My wrist is broken," Nantz joked after visibly appearing to hurt his hand following a full punch on the ball, all while Watt sympathetically laughed in the background. "Like I'm going to knock it out of your hands."

Watt was best known for rushing the quarterback during his career, but don't forget that he also had three offensive touchdowns as a red-zone receiving threat. The man has good hands (to go alongside his brute strength).

articles.title: DeForest Buckner 'Sick and Tired' of Colts' Losses, Sounds Off on Loss to Titans in Video
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts haven't been to the playoffs since 2020, and after dropping to 2-4 with a loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, it appears the streak might continue this year.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts haven't been to the playoffs since 2020, and after dropping to 2-4 with a loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, it appears the streak might continue this year.

Veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is getting exhausted by his team's constant struggles.

"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters after the loss.

The Colts appeared to be turning the corner last year after a 7-2 start, but ultimately ended the year 8-9 and missed the playoffs. Now, Indianapolis' playoff hopes are already dwindling, and Buckner is ready for something to change.
