articles.title: Bears get a massive Caleb Williams boost at exactly the right time
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams are showing the NFL one thing in his comeback game.
articles.body:
It certainly didn't come too soon and really happened just in the nick of time, but the Chicago Bears got quarterback Caleb Williams back right when they needed him most.

The Bears fell hard to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5 of the NFL season on Oct. 11, and it was a gut punch to a franchise that finally has hope after years of being at the bottom. Now, in Week 6, the Bears got Williams back on the field, and he helped lead this team to a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons . It's just the boost this franchise needed going into its next handful of games.

Caleb Williams returns with an 'ultra-efficient' performance for the Bears

Coming out of the NFL's Week 6 games , Dan Parr of the NFL's official website noted that not only is Williams back, but he's "ultra-efficient."

"What a difference a week makes," he adds. "Last Sunday, Ben Johnson's team was blown out in Green Bay. On Sunday, it was the Bears who dominated for most of the game. They outgained the Falcons, 154-3 in the first quarter, marching out to a 14-0 lead with their QB1, Caleb Williams, setting the tone."

The Falcons were able to make a comeback in the fourth quarter, but it wasn't quite enough to put them in the win column. Meanwhile, Williams was 30 of 36 for 305 yards and had a touchdown in his first game back since his hamstring injury in Week 2. He also had an 83% completion rate, which, according to Parr, is the "highest in a game by a Bears QB to attempt at least 30 passes in franchise history."

"While Williams only had four rushing attempts for 3 yards, his ability to extend plays with his legs was on full display," getting rid of "any concerns about seeing a significantly reduced version of the face of the franchise post-injury," he added.

It wasn't a perfect game, and the Bears had 12 penalties, which is a lot. But it was a promising showing for a franchise that has its on-field leader back.

articles.title: Former Lions DB C.J. Gardner-Johnson Ejected For Spitting
articles.summary: Former Detroit Lions safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the Bills-Raiders game after spitting toward Brock Bowers. Watch the incident.
articles.body:
Former Detroit Lions defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson found himself in the middle of another controversy Sunday afternoon, and this one brought his day to an early end. The current Buffalo Bills safety was ejected for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers during the second quarter of their Week 6 matchup.

The incident occurred late in the first half as the Raiders were driving into Buffalo territory. Following an exchange between Gardner-Johnson and several Las Vegas players, officials flagged the veteran defensive back for unsportsmanlike conduct and announced his disqualification.

According to reporting on the incident , Gardner-Johnson appeared to spit toward Bowers during the confrontation. The moment was captured on video, leaving the Bills without one of their defensive backs for the remainder of the game.

C.J. Gardner-Johnson's Latest Controversy Could Bring NFL Discipline

For Lions fans, Gardner-Johnson's involvement in another on-field controversy might bring back memories of his brief stint in Detroit. The veteran safety spent the 2023 season with the Lions before returning to Philadelphia, and his outspoken personality has continued to attract attention throughout his NFL career.

As we previously documented , Gardner-Johnson generated headlines for a controversial wardrobe choice during Philadelphia's Super Bowl celebration in 2025. Sunday's incident, however, goes beyond trash talk or attention-grabbing comments because it resulted in an immediate ejection.

The NFL could review the play for additional discipline, although no further punishment had been announced when this article was prepared. Gardner-Johnson was also among several Buffalo players fined by the league following last week's game , making Sunday's ejection another potentially costly development.

Gardner-Johnson's latest disqualification also adds to his history of on-field disciplinary issues. As we previously covered in another Lions-related NFL discipline story , the league can impose additional financial penalties after reviewing conduct that occurred during a game.

For Buffalo, the immediate consequence was losing Gardner-Johnson for the remainder of Sunday's matchup. Whether the NFL decides to impose an additional fine or suspension will be determined through its disciplinary review process.

articles.title: Tanner McKee struggles in place of injured Jalen Hurts and Eagles have first 4-game skid since 2020
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Tanner McKee still had a chance in the fourth quarter to win a game for the Eagles. Despite a series of failed screen and swing passes an...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Tanner McKee still had a chance in the fourth quarter to win a game for the Eagles. Despite a series of failed screen and swing passes and a stagnant running game, McKee had his first game-winning drive in sight on Sunday in his first start this season for the injured Jalen Hurts .

McKee had hit DeVonta Smith for a 19-yard touchdown pass that cut Philadelphia's deficit to five points. The defense did its part, holding Bryce Young and Carolina to a three-and-out that gave the Eagles the ball at their 48-yard line with 9:32 left.

McKee, a sixth-round pick who spent four seasons backing up Hurts, so badly wanted to meet the moment.

Not this season, which is quickly falling apart for the Eagles.

Philadelphia had a botched snap on first down and McKee fell on the ball for a 12-yard loss. McKee's third-down pass was deflected and fell incomplete.

Braden Mann's punt was blocked, and the Panthers got the ball at midfield.

Young threw his second touchdown pass of the game, the final blow in the Eagles' fourth straight loss, 25-14 to the Panthers .

"It's really hard to win in the NFL," McKee said, "only putting up 14 points."

The Eagles (2-4) have lost four consecutive games for the first time since 2020. Coach Nick Sirianni took over the following season.

McKee finished 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown. Hurts attempted 40 passes only once this season and three times never got above 27 attempts.

"I am so much better, and I'm looking forward to learning everything and becoming the player that I know I am, the player that I can prove that I am," McKee said.

The Eagles only had 222 yards of offense. McKee was sacked three times. Philadelphia punted on five straight possessions to start the game.

"You've got to score points, and we're not doing that right now," Sirianni said.

McKee was sacked for an 11-yard loss on the Eagles' first play from scrimmage and he nearly had a pass intercepted on second down. The 26-year-old's outing never got much better, and it's easy to wonder just how the Eagles can salvage their season.

"Everything's on the table," Sirianni said.

Hurts will miss at least three more games after he was placed on injured reserve Saturday, two days after the Eagles revealed he has a blood clot in his calf .

Hurts hadn't missed more than two games in a season since becoming the full-time starter in 2021. He's led the Eagles to five straight playoff appearances, three NFC East titles, two Super Bowl appearances and one title.

The Eagles will need to go 7-4 to have a sixth straight winning season under Sirianni.

"There's always an urgency," Sirianni said. "You can be calm when there's an urgency."

Sirianni might not want to turn on Philadelphia sports radio or scan social media comments. Calm is not an option.

In the first meaningful start of his NFL career, McKee didn't turn the ball over and never let the game get out of reach until the fourth quarter. He should have time to improve and get comfortable with more practice reps as the No. 1 QB.

"I think we can mold it to my strengths and mold it to what we do well as an offense," McKee said. "We have a lot of really good playmakers. And so I think it's just whatever our offense will do best this week versus whoever we're playing."

Hurts is one of a handful of sidelined starters for the Eagles.

Saquon Barkley, a 2,000-yard rusher during their Super Bowl championship season, missed his second straight game with a hamstring injury. Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby, his two backups, were also sidelined by injuries. Carson Steele, who was signed off the practice squad last week, left early with a shoulder injury.

Dameon Pierce was the only Eagles running back to get a carry against a Panthers defense that came in having allowed the 30th-most yards rushing per game. He rushed for 35 yards and scored on a 2-yard run to cut Carolina's lead to 10-7 at halftime.

One silver lining for the rest of the Eagles' season: They play in the worst division in football.

Last week, all four NFC East teams played, including two against each other, and none of them won . The New York Giants lead the division at 3-2-1 after losing 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday .

The Eagles host Dallas on Monday, Oct. 26.

"I'd like to think I'm an optimist," offensive tackle Jordan Mailata said. "The message this week was pretty simple. Maybe I need to change it: Where there's adversity, there's an opportunity. We need to take that and run with that."

articles.title: 4 things we learned from the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints
articles.summary: With resurgent Houston on deck, the party’s over
articles.body:
It's an annual tradition. How long do we have to wait for the first MetLife stinker of the year by the New York Giants? In 2023 and 2024, the Giants got that out of the way in their opening game. In 2025, it wasn't until the Kansas City game in week 3, but that was only because the first two games were on the road; it was still the first home game.

This year, things were different for a while at MetLife: A stirring opening win over Dallas, then two squeakers over bad Titans and Cardinals teams but in poor weather conditions. Today, the weather was beautiful at MetLife, and it looked like the Giants might be on their way to another home win. They jumped out to a 10-0 lead against the New Orleans Saints and were controlling the game. Then Daniel Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:16 left in the first half. Charlie Jones fumbled on the ensuing kickoff, and it was all downhill from there, to the tune of 34 consecutive points by New Orleans.

Yet the score wound up 34-27, and the Giants were within one end zone play of sending the game to overtime. What did we learn from this infuriating loss, the Giants' fourth in four years to one of the NFC's bottom feeders?

I just do not like the Matt Nagy offense. Up to this point he's run too often on first down, and usually between the tackles. It's not getting the offense anywhere. More on that in a minute. But first, the passing game:

Zero pass attempts beyond 20 yards for Jameis Winston. Only two pass attempts outside the hash marks at intermediate depths. And this against one of the poorer pass defenses in the NFL. For some perspective, let's look at the same chart for Winston from last year in the Brian Daboll-Mike Kafka offense:

Notice the ball being distributed all over the field. Other than Martin Emerson Jr., a good but not great cornerback, the rest of the Saints' secondary is ordinary at best.

And it's not just the passing depths. It seems to me that almost every pass attempt is a contested catch opportunity rather than a route that is designed to create conflicts in the defense. I'm seeing a lot of stuff into the flat with no blockers in front of the receiver. I'm not seeing the high-low route combinations, the intermediate crossers, etc. that are the staple of explosive offenses.

Finally when J.J. McCarthy came into the game, we saw some passes downfield (other than his first brief appearance, when Nagy had him run another one of those useless RPOs). By then, though, he had no choice and the Saints were playing soft to not give up the big play (which they actually did not do very well). Whether J.J.'s performance has created a quarterback controversy or not, I don't know. What I do know, though, is that Winston is not being given a fair chance to show what he can do in the ultra-conservative, unimaginative offense he's been asked to run.

Malik Nabers had 165 yards on 12 catches today…but many of those came after the Giants fell behind. Isaiah Likely caught six passes for 99 yards. Between them, Darnell Mooney, and Malachi Fields, it should be possible to run up big passing yards before you get to the fourth quarter. Try it, Matt.

I'm sure Cam Skattebo has learned his lesson…has John Harbaugh learned his?

I get it. Skattebo has fumbled four times already this season, and his last one cost the Giants a victory in Washington. I'm all for a little discipline to get a point across to a player (and to his teammates). But there's an old expression about cutting off your nose to spite your face. John Harbaugh cut the nose off the Giants' offense by effectively benching Cam Skattebo, the Giants' best running back, for the entire game. Najee Harris (four carries, 2 yards) is not the answer. Tyrone Tracy (six carries, 18 yards, but a TD and also two receptions for 27 yards and a TD) is part of the answer. Devin Singletary (four carries, 14 yards and a 19-yard reception) can be part of it, too.

But Cam Skattebo is the Giants' lead back. You want to teach him a lesson? Let him sit for the first quarter, or even the first half. Point made, point taken. But once the Saints had changed the momentum and the teams went in at halftime tied, it was time to get Skattebo back into the lineup to give the offense a jolt. Skattebo did play six snaps, but he didn't touch the ball once. Giants' running backs accounted for a total of 34 yards against one of the NFL's worst rushing defenses. The Giants' run blocking is bad, but these Next Gen Stats tell us that the running backs are a big part of the problem:

If only D.J. Reader could play every snap

As opposed to the Giants' anemic running game, the Saints' running backs racked up 143 rushing yards today. It seemed to me that most of those came either when D.J. Reader was off the field or when they didn't rush to his side. Every time I saw a Saints' RB stuffed, It seemed I saw #98. He made 7 tackles overall (5 solo, 2 assists). Shelby Harris, who is usually on the field with him, seemed to play fairly well too ( 1 tackle, 2 assists).

The run defense degrades considerably when Reader is off the field. Darius Alexander (1 tackle, 0 assists) at this point is a real liability in run defense. I don't know what the Giants can do about it, other than get far enough ahead that teams are forced to abandon the run. Until they can, though, this will continue to be a problem.

Other than the kicker and punter, the special teams are not special

Jordan Stout has been as advertised, and Dominic Zvada seems not to have been shaken too much by his three missed field goals last week in Washington. The Giants return teams, however, have been awful. The game-turning play was obviously Charlie Jones' fumble on the kickoff late in the first half, which allowed the Saints to tie the score at the half.

But that's not all. It seemed to me that every time the Giants had a kickoff or punt to return it was called back by a penalty. Overall the Giants had 10 penalties for 73 yards to the Saints' 7 for 52. I'm not sure how many of those were on special teams, but I'm not the only one who thinks it's a problem:

For someone who earned his chops as a special teams coordinator before becoming a head coach, Harbaugh has a very undisciplined return unit.

The shame of all this is that the Giants now go into Houston to face the resurgent Texans at 3-2-1 rather than the 5-1 they should have been.

articles.title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson ejected for spitting on Brock Bowers in latest controversy involving Bills safety
articles.summary: Gardner-Johnson drew the referees' rebuke after appearing to attempt to spit on Raiders star Brock Bowers.
articles.body:
C.J. Gardner-Johnson has rarely avoided the spotlight across his eight-year NFL career. He had no problem continuing that trend on Sunday evening.

The Bills safety was banished from Buffalo's Week 6 clash with the Raiders , drawing the referee's ire after getting into it with Las Vegas star Brock Bowers. A closer look at their dust-up revealed that Gardner-Johnson was more than deserving of his punishment.

C.J. Gardner-Johnson ejected for spitting on Brock Bowers

Gardner-Johnson was served his walking papers shortly before halftime commenced. Buffalo's starting safety was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct after jawing with Bowers, leading to his dismissal.

At first, it was unclear why Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the contest. Trash talk is a regular occurrence across the NFL. Rarely does it draw the referee's whistles.

Replay of the incident revealed just why Gardner-Johnson was banished to the locker room, however. Gardner-Johnson appeared to attempt to spit on Bowers.

Tyler Linderbaum was alert to the act, calling the umpire over the investigate the biological attack. His flag would fly moments later.

Gardner-Johnson's actions would draw rebuke from a host of different personalities, including CBS' broadcast crew. Nate Burleson and Bill Cowher called out the veteran for his act, labeling it as a dereliction of his duty as a Bills player.

Damar Hamlin replaced Gardner-Johnson in Buffalo's secondary. The ejection represents the second of Gardner-Johnson's professional career; as a member of the Eagles , he was tossed in a 2024 tilt with the Commanders after receiving two unsportsmanlike conduct flags.

articles.title: Bills safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson ejected against Raiders
articles.summary: Bills cornerback Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game against the Raiders for spitting.
articles.body:
Buffalo safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the Bills at Raiders game in the second quarter for spitting at an opposing player.

The unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, was enforced as half the distance to the goal line with 15 seconds before the half. The Bills led Las Vegas 13-10 at the time.

Las Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins had just thrown an incompletion on third down from the 33, but a different Bills player got flagged for holding. Then Gardner-Johnson's incident occurred between plays in the aftermath.

Video appeared to show Gardner-Johnson spitting at Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Las Vegas lineman Tyler Linderbaum, standing nearby, immediately appealed to the officials.

Bowers and Gardner-Johnson were jawing at each other after a play and after Bowers turned his back to head to the huddle, CBS cameras caught Gardner-Johnson spitting in the tight end's direction.

Gardner-Johnson was escorted to the locker room with 15 seconds left in the half. Las Vegas eventually kicked a field goal on the drive to tie the score, 13-13.

Per Quirky Research's database on NFL ejections, this is the first time Gardner-Johnson has been tossed in the league.

However, in 2020, Jacksonville native Javon Wims from got ejected for punching Gardner-Johnson during a Bears - Saints game.

This is the first NFL ejection for spitting in the database since Jalen Carter of Philadelphia against the Cowboys at the start of the 2025 season.

Gardner-Johnson is a graduate of Cocoa High School and the University of Florida. He won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles after the 2024 season.

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Job Security Addressed by Colts' Shane Steichen After Shocking Loss to Titans
articles.summary: Despite falling to 2-4 after Sunday's 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans, Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen isn't giving up on starting quarterback Daniel Jones.
articles.body:
Despite falling to 2-4 after Sunday's 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans, Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen isn't giving up on starting quarterback Daniel Jones.

When asked after Sunday's loss about Jones' status as the team's starter, Steichen made it clear that he isn't planning on making any drastic changes.

"Yes, he is our starting quarterback," Steichen affirmed.

Jones was 22-of-42 for 269 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's game. He was sacked six times by a Titans team that had only 10 sacks through the first five weeks of the season.

Steichen said that Jones isn't the sole person to blame for the Colts' struggles this year.

"I think he knows he's gotta play better. I've gotta coach better," he said. "There's a lot of things, it's not on one guy. We've gotta do a lot of things better."

The Colts will try to address their deficiencies before they return to action in Week 7 against the Minnesota Vikings (5-0).

articles.title: Viral Preseason Quote from Cardinals' Mack Wilson Resurfaces After Upset Win vs. Rams
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams came into the season as Super Bowl favorites, and the rebuilding Arizona Cardinals were the least of their worries.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams came into the season as Super Bowl favorites, and the rebuilding Arizona Cardinals were the least of their worries.

But Cardinals linebacker Mack Wilson knew his squad was not to be overlooked. After Arizona upset the Rams on Sunday, a preseason quote from Wilson resurfaced.

"They've got to deal with us," Wilson told reporters before the season started. "At the end of the day, they've got to deal with us."

Wilson's quote wasn't just confidence, but manifestation. The Cardinals came into Sunday's matchup on a four-game losing streak, but left SoFi Stadium with an 18-16 victory.

Now, instead of being Super Bowl contenders, the Rams are hoping to regroup and make the playoffs. Los Angeles dropped to 2-4 on Sunday and sits in last place in the NFC West.

The Rams had a tough slate to begin the season, facing the San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos and the Buffalo Bills. They would have liked to have made it through that stretch with more than two wins, but they will now have to turn things around moving forward.

Things don't get much easier next week, as Los Angeles faces a Las Vegas Raiders team that has looked solid through its first six games.
